acknowledgedReviews.subject: widgets/quick-controls
acknowledgedReviews.reason: The live display controls (monitor strip, K/% readout, temperature + brightness sliders, auto day/night, the eight preset modes) kept standalone: Settings → Display is its only consumer today, but this block IS the removed main window, and the tray flyout renders the same controls off the same features/display seam — a reusable composite, not a page detail.

acknowledgedReviews.subject: features/rules
acknowledgedReviews.reason: Per-app rules feature (pure rule-model, running-window picker, add/edit dialog, i18n labels) kept standalone: the settings window's Rules panel is its only consumer today, but it is a self-contained slice reusable by any window and independently unit-tested — not folded into the page.

acknowledgedReviews.subject: features/display
acknowledgedReviews.reason: Display control feature (value/patch logic, settings persistence, live-preview driver, monitor + engine-state hooks) kept standalone: three independent surfaces drive it — the quick-controls widget, the tray flyout and the Rust hotkey actions — so it belongs to none of them.

acknowledgedReviews.subject: features/hotkey-actions
acknowledgedReviews.reason: Display hotkey-action catalogue + pure hotkey-patch/validation logic kept standalone: the settings window's Hotkeys panel is its only frontend consumer today, but the action ids are the shared contract with the Rust registry (armed from settings, fired via hotkey:triggered) and the slice is independently unit-tested — not folded into the page.

acknowledgedReviews.subject: features/auto-dark
acknowledgedReviews.reason: Auto Dark feature (autoDark settings persistence through the shared serialized save coordinator) kept standalone: the settings window's Auto Dark panel is its only consumer today, but it is a reusable slice owning the frontend save path for the magicx::theme backend scheduler (Windows app/system theme + taskbar transparency) — paralleling features/display, not folded into the page.

acknowledgedReviews.subject: features/record-hotkey
acknowledgedReviews.reason: Global-shortcut recorder (key capture, conflict detection, the recorder UI) kept standalone: the settings window's Hotkeys panel is its only consumer here, but this slice is shared verbatim across DimRead, the starter template and WinSTT — folding it into the page would fork the one implementation the three repos replicate fixes between.
